changes: The introduction is the record: each observation takes its words, and the essays are no longer a source.

O2 is the introduction's: pressure and focused attention release knots one place at a time, and pressed, with a slow out-breath, a knot often lets go within seconds. The draft's 'pressure, then release, lets go faster than calm alone' was the vessel model's trial, not a report.
O2b (focus alone) is folded into O2, where the introduction puts attention: with pressure.
O16 is added from the introduction: some knots come and go with breath and mood.
O14 (clusters at the base of the skull; warmth from an old cluster) is set aside: it is only in the essays. Where knots gather is in O4.
The readings of the words and the scoring rules are fixed here, so that no reading can be stretched to fit a model.

observations.title: Breath release
observations.text: Knots answer to the breath: they let go on a slow out-breath. A single relaxing breath, the long exhale that comes on its own in a hot shower, can soften many small knots at once; deeper, persistent knots let go only to focused attention and breath. Release can be broad or focused. Easy knots go within a breath or two; hard ones take many breaths. The breath is a learned skill, proprioceptive and meditative.

words.quote: Knots seem to answer to the breath. They let go on a slow out-breath, and a single relaxing breath — the long exhale that comes on its own in a hot shower — can soften many small knots at once.
deeper, persistent knots let go only to focused attention and breath.
breath (i believe a complex proprioceptive meditative breath that is a learned skill) releases knots and can be broad or focused.
who knows if some knots take multiple breaths to work on. Vs other easier ones.

observations.note: How the breath acts is left open: drive, movement, local nerves, attention and chemistry are variants, not assumptions.

observations.title: Pressure and attention
observations.text: Pressure and focused attention, a foam roller or a patient hand, release knots one place at a time. Pressed, with a slow out-breath, a knot often lets go within seconds.

words.quote: Press into a knot, breathe out slowly, and it often lets go within seconds.
Pressure and focused attention — a foam roller, a patient hand — release knots one place at a time.

observations.title: Water
observations.text: Drinking water seems to ease release, and to speed it.

words.quote: Drinking water seems to ease release, and to speed it.

observations.note: Most theories are expected to be silent; silence is reported as silence.

observations.title: Stress
observations.text: Knots worsen under stress, and gather where it is held: neck and shoulders, jaw, belly, low back.

words.quote: Knots seem to worsen under stress, and gather where it is held: neck and shoulders, jaw, belly, low back.

observations.title: Coming and going
observations.text: Some knots come and go with breath and mood; some may even be held from moment to moment.

words.quote: Some knots seem to come and go with breath and mood, and some may even be held from moment to moment

observations.title: Stiffness
observations.text: As knots gather they limit movement. A stretch is felt as a clear, sharp pull in the muscle, but it meets the knots as dull, deep blocks it cannot reach.

words.quote: As knots gather they seem to limit movement. A stretch is felt as a clear, sharp pull in the muscle, but it meets the knots as dull, deep blocks it cannot reach.

observations.title: Sparks
observations.text: A knot goes with a small pop, sometimes a star of tingling across a patch of skin.

words.quote: A knot goes with a small pop, sometimes a star of tingling across a patch of skin.

observations.note: The measurement that tells theories apart is spatial: overbreathing makes tingling anywhere, so only tingling confined to the released knot's own patch discriminates.

observations.title: Migration
observations.text: When one knot lets go, others move in to fill the gap and settle into new places, as if the body were evening itself out.

words.quote: When one knot lets go, others move in to fill the gap and settle into new places, as if the body were evening itself out.

observations.title: A parent releases its children
observations.text: Releasing one knot (a parent) lets many others (its children) go with it.

words.quote: Clustering can be an observation - parent release many children. I’ve felt this.

observations.note: Written down on 26 Sep 2026, after the tree simulation had been shared: the vascular tree's match is found after the fact, not predicted blind. How many children, how soon, where they lie and what stays are the blind tests.

observations.title: Sizes and numbers
observations.text: Knots come in a hierarchy: a few large knots that take many sessions to clear, and micro knots at dozens to the square inch, hundreds of thousands in a body by practitioners' own estimate.

words.quote: Those who count describe a hierarchy: a few large knots that take many sessions to clear, and micro-knots at dozens to the square inch — hundreds of thousands in a body, by their own estimate.
words.from: the introduction, A ladder of a hundred thousand

observations.note: The number and density are part of the test: each theory predicts its own, and only a unit that dense can host a micro knot.

observations.title: Mirroring
observations.text: Working the knots on one side can ease the other side as well.

words.quote: Working the knots on one side can ease the other side as well.

observations.note: The crossover effect of rolling or stretching one side is measured; a scoping review puts it down most likely to reduced pain perception.

observations.title: Age
observations.text: Knots accumulate with age, and they grow; the young have few. A young knot is small and comes and goes; an old one is larger and persists, and as they gather the body stiffens.

words.quote: Knots accumulate with age, and they grow. The young have few.
A young knot is small and comes and goes; an old one is larger and persists, and as they gather the body stiffens.

observations.title: Euphoria
observations.text: A release can bring a wave of well-being, at times a euphoria some compare to MDMA.

words.quote: A release can bring a wave of well-being — at times a euphoria some compare to MDMA.

observations.note: Out of scope for tissue-level models.

observations.title: Peeling and filling
observations.text: Layers of the fascia beneath the skin can peel apart along lines, leaving places that feel hollow, rarely; then a filling-in, felt as re-stitching, that can move like a snake along a limb, up the body, or up into the head.

words.quote: Some have reported layers of the fascia beneath the skin peeling apart along lines, leaving places that feel hollow. It is rare and little understood
Then a filling-in, felt as re-stitching, that can move like a snake along a limb, up the body, or up into the head.

set_aside: Releases run along paths that converge on the back of the skull, where knots are released and then replaced, as if from a queue.
Knots cluster most at the base of the skull, and an old, heavily loaded cluster can let go with a wave of warmth spreading from the site.
Distant places (the brow, the temple, the jaw, the side of the nose) can unlock a stubborn region at the ridge of the skull.
Pressure alone does not seem to release a knot.
Fresh knots yield in a session; old ones take months.
The knots go first: the fascia's separating cannot begin at a site until its knots are gone.

scoring: Each part of an observation is scored on its own: pass, fail, or silent.
A theory with no account of a part is silent on it. Silence is shown as silence, never counted as a pass or a fail.
A pass is reported as the share of plausible parameter sets in which the part holds, never as one tuned setting.
Observations in the group 'noted' are shown and not scored; the set-aside reports are shown and not scored.
